title: Chapter 10 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of transfer learning, pretrained models, and fine‑tuning!

questions.question: What is transfer learning?
options: Training a model from scratch on a new dataset
Reusing knowledge from a pretrained model to solve a different but related task
Converting a model to ONNX format
questions.explanation: Transfer learning leverages pre‑learned features for a new task, reducing data and training time.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of transfer learning?
options: Eliminates the need for any training
Leverages features learned from large datasets
questions.explanation: You still need to train the adapted model on the target data, though often for fewer epochs.

questions.question: Which method freezes all pretrained layers and trains only a new classifier?
questions.explanation: Feature extraction keeps the backbone fixed.

questions.question: How do you load a pretrained ResNet18 with default weights in the latest PyTorch API?
questions.explanation: The new API uses `weights` parameter with an enum.

questions.question: When using feature extraction, you can simply replace the final fully connected layer and train it.
questions.explanation: Yes, you freeze the backbone and retrain the head.

questions.question: To freeze a layer's parameters, set `param.________ = False`.
questions.explanation: Set `requires_grad=False` to exclude parameters from gradient computation.

questions.question: What is the typical learning rate for the new head compared to the pretrained backbone during fine‑tuning?
questions.explanation: The new head usually has a higher learning rate because its weights are randomly initialized.

questions.question: Which PyTorch method returns the preprocessing transforms associated with a pretrained model?
questions.explanation: `weights.transforms()` gives the required preprocessing (resize, center crop, normalize).

questions.question: In ResNet18, what is the name of the final classification layer?
questions.explanation: ResNet models use `model.fc` for the final linear layer.

questions.question: What does `in_features` of the original fc layer represent?
options: The input feature dimension from the feature extractor
questions.explanation: It's the size of the feature vector coming into the classifier.

questions.question: Why might you unfreeze only the last few layers of a pretrained model during fine‑tuning?
options: To adapt high‑level features to the new dataset while preserving low‑level features
To reduce the number of parameters
questions.explanation: Early layers capture generic features; later layers capture task‑specific details that may need adaptation.

questions.question: Which optimizer feature allows different learning rates for different parameter groups?
options: Passing a list of dicts with 'params' and 'lr' keys
Using a single learning rate for all
questions.explanation: You can specify per‑group learning rates in PyTorch optimizers.

questions.question: Fine‑tuning requires a larger dataset than feature extraction.
questions.explanation: Fine‑tuning updates more parameters, so more data is needed to avoid overfitting.

questions.question: Which dataset is commonly used to pretrain vision models?
questions.explanation: ImageNet (1.2M images, 1000 classes) is the standard pretraining dataset.

questions.question: After you replace `model.fc` with a new Linear layer, are its parameters trainable by default?
options: No, you must set it manually
It inherits the previous layer's setting
questions.explanation: Newly created modules have `requires_grad=True` by default.

questions.question: What is the risk of using too high a learning rate during fine‑tuning?
questions.explanation: Large weight updates can distort the useful pretrained filters.

questions.question: What does `torchvision.models.resnet18(weights=None)` do?
options: Loads a randomly initialized ResNet18 (no pretraining)
questions.explanation: `weights=None` gives a fresh, untrained model.

questions.question: When using `ImageFolder` for custom data, how are labels assigned?
questions.explanation: `ImageFolder` treats subfolder names as class labels, sorted alphabetically.

questions.question: Which learning rate scheduler is often used during fine‑tuning to reduce LR on plateau?
questions.explanation: ReduceLROnPlateau lowers LR when validation loss stops improving.

questions.question: You can fine‑tune a model trained on ImageNet for medical image classification.
questions.explanation: Yes, even though domains differ, low‑level features transfer, and fine‑tuning adapts higher‑level features.
